mcqs.q: In an Italian shelter, what was the main effect of a 4-month behavioral training program on adoption outcomes?
o: Higher adoption numbers of adult and senior dogs
Shorter stays for aggressive dogs only
mcqs.e: Trained adult and senior dogs were adopted in greater numbers than untrained age-matched controls.

mcqs.q: What did the authors conclude about training and the human-animal bond?
o: Training improves dogs' natural attitudes and supports a better bond
Training had no measurable behavioral benefit
Bonding depends only on dog age
mcqs.e: They concluded training improves companion dogs' natural attitudes, strengthening the human-animal bond.

mcqs.q: Over 20 years, which presenting complaint was most common at the behavior service?
mcqs.e: Aggression accounted for 72.2% of cases, far exceeding other categories.

mcqs.q: How did the sources of dogs presenting for behavior problems change over 20 years?
o: More came from shelters, rescues, or strays
mcqs.e: Breeder-sourced dogs decreased while shelter/rescue/stray-sourced dogs increased (p<0.0001).

mcqs.q: Which breed groups were overrepresented among behavior cases?
mcqs.e: Herding (p=0.0124) and Terrier (p<0.0001) groups were overrepresented versus all other services.

mcqs.q: During negative situations, owner-rated heightened arousal correlated with which physiological pattern?
o: Lower HRV with more fear behaviors
mcqs.e: Heightened arousal was linked to lower HRV, higher activity, and more fear/arousal behaviors.

mcqs.q: Which MDORS factor was associated with increased HRV, suggesting a secure-base effect?
mcqs.e: Emotional Closeness correlated with increased HRV (p=0.009), consistent with a secure-base effect.

mcqs.q: What overall conclusion did the authors reach?
o: Emotional reactivity and the dog-owner relationship mutually modulate each other
Relationship quality has no effect on reactivity
mcqs.e: They concluded emotional reactivity and the dog-owner relationship modulate one another.

mcqs.q: What is the main welfare consequence of inadequate puppy socialisation per the review?
o: Higher risk of problematic adult behaviours
mcqs.e: Poorly socialised puppies have a higher risk of problem behaviours in adulthood.

mcqs.q: Why are modern controlled studies using unsocialised controls lacking?
o: They would now be considered unethical
mcqs.e: Early work showed socialisation's importance so clearly that unsocialised-control studies are deemed unethical.

mcqs.q: What research priority did the review recommend?
o: Minimum necessary socialisation levels and breed timing differences
mcqs.e: Authors call for research on minimum necessary socialisation and breed-specific timing.

mcqs.q: What behavior did 1- and 2-month-old puppies show toward humans?
mcqs.e: Puppies exhibited locomotor synchrony with human walking.

mcqs.q: How did familiarity with the human affect the puppies' synchrony?
o: It did not affect the degree of synchrony
mcqs.e: Familiarity did not influence the degree of synchrony in the puppies.

mcqs.q: What does this finding suggest about the origin of dog-human synchronization?
o: It is purely learned in adulthood
It appears genetically selected through domestication
It is unique to familiar dyads
mcqs.e: Early, familiarity-independent synchrony suggests selection via domestication, with familiarity effects developing later.

mcqs.q: The review frames early-life risk factors using which concept?
o: Developmental origins of health and disease (DOHaD)
mcqs.e: It applies the DOHaD/developmental-programming framework to dogs and cats.

mcqs.q: Which adult disorders are highlighted as having early-life risk factors?
o: Obesity, chronic enteropathy, and behavioral problems
mcqs.e: The review covers obesity, chronic enteropathy, and chronic behavioral problems.

mcqs.q: What major barrier to DOHaD research in dogs and cats is identified?
o: Breed variability and discontinuity of husbandry between breeders and owners
Animals live too briefly to study
mcqs.e: Wide breed variability and fragmented husbandry/ownership hinder lifelong cohort studies.

mcqs.q: Anticipatory behavior is proposed as an animal-based measure related to what?
mcqs.e: Anticipatory behavior is theorized to reflect animals' reward sensitivity.

mcqs.q: What risk do the authors warn about when interpreting space- and time-use data?
o: Unidentified anticipation leading to misleading welfare conclusions
mcqs.e: Failing to identify anticipation can produce misleading conclusions about behavior or welfare.

mcqs.q: Why is the managed/captive environment conducive to anticipatory behavior?
mcqs.e: The predictability of managed environments fosters development of anticipatory behaviors.

mcqs.q: What compulsive behavior did the German Shepherd mix present with?
mcqs.e: The dog presented with tail chasing, a common canine compulsive trait, with self-inflicted wounds.

mcqs.q: Which pharmacological agents were used in the treatment?
mcqs.e: Treatment combined fluoxetine with alpha-s1 casozepine plus a behavioral recovery program.

mcqs.q: What outcome followed the interdisciplinary treatment?
o: Reduced intensity/frequency and eventual cessation of episodes
mcqs.e: Compulsive events decreased and no new tail-chasing episodes occurred over the following 3 months.

mcqs.q: What was the main aim of the study with unsocialised stray dogs?
o: Determine if rehabilitation/training could make them adoptable
mcqs.e: The study tested whether rehabilitation and training could build the skills needed for adoption.

mcqs.q: How did the stray dogs' sociability toward humans change?
o: It improved from ST1 to ST3
mcqs.e: Stray dogs' sociability toward humans improved across the testing time-points.

mcqs.q: What did the authors note about individual variation among the strays?
o: Large variation: some stayed fearful while others became handleable
mcqs.e: There was large individual variation; some strays remained intensely fearful while others could be leash-walked.

mcqs.q: Which factors were significantly associated with aggression incidence in Brazilian pet dogs?
o: Dog weight, skull morphology, sex, and socio-environmental factors
mcqs.e: Weight, skull morphology, sex, owner gender/age, training regimen, and household factors affected aggression.

mcqs.q: Which measure was NOT associated with aggression?
mcqs.e: Aggression was not associated with BMI, the measure used to represent dog size.

mcqs.q: What overall view of aggression do the results support?
o: A single species- or breed-wide cause
A multifactorial interaction of genetics, physiology, experience, and environment
mcqs.e: Results reinforce aggression as a multifactorial trait emerging from interacting developmental factors.

mcqs.q: Compared with other shelter dogs, dogs from adverse early backgrounds had what cortisol pattern?
mcqs.e: Dogs from adverse backgrounds showed significantly higher salivary cortisol (p=0.045).

mcqs.q: During interactions with an unfamiliar human, adverse-background dogs showed which behavior?
o: More fear and less affiliative behavior
mcqs.e: They displayed more fear and lower affiliative behavior than other shelter dogs.

mcqs.q: Did time in adverse conditions or time in the shelter correlate with cortisol output?
mcqs.e: Neither duration in adverse conditions nor time in the shelter correlated with cortisol output.

mcqs.q: What effect did partial visual barrier removal have on vocalizations?
o: Lower vocalizations in the visual-access and post phases
mcqs.e: Vocalizations were lower during the visual-access and post phases (p=.02), and barking duration did not increase.

mcqs.q: What happened to stress behaviors and resting behaviors across phases?
mcqs.e: Stress behaviors, crate position, and resting behaviors did not differ significantly across phases.

mcqs.q: What did the authors recommend shelters prioritize for welfare?
o: Increased social contact via playgroups or group housing
mcqs.e: Because visual contact alone seemed insufficient, they recommend playgroups or group housing.
